questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: language

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Most of it was easy - but the information from my home university was sometimes quite different than the one received by the visiting university, which made it difficult. Another difficult part was doing the online learning agreement and the pre-approval of courses, since courses get updated very late (1/7) and my home university is closed throughout July, so I didn't get my OLA approved before leaving.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: not any specific assistance.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: everything was something you had to choose to attend yourself. It was also difficult understanding the difference between the international check in and the proof of attendance - many people mixed them up and only attended one of them.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: we found it 6 months prior to going, so it was easy.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: its expensive and be prepared not getting your deposit back as well as aware of getting scammed by your landlord.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: didn't look into it.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: we had to go to one office to register that we had arrived and then also book an international check in. It was smooth whilst doing it, but difficult figuring out the practicality beforehand

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: visiting student office by e-mail

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: got all my courses

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: expect that courses you've put into your first pre-approval will be different ones you end up taking. they'll put in the updated courses in july in the course catalouge. Don't spent to much time finding good courses the first time.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer:
same level as UCPH. 2/3 of my courses were third year undergraduate / first year postgraduate. These were the same levels as UCPH. 
Took one course made for second year undergraduate, but a different subject than my main one in UCPH, which made the level appropriate as well. I had two essays per course for the semester, which meant a total og 6 exams, which is more than i'm used to. The exams were "practical coursework" which means essays of 1000-3000 words, with a self-made question or you get handed one. The essays are like discussion papers, and not research papers which we mostly do at UCPH. it's not that difficult, just a different writing style. Most semester I spent on doing essays, since the semester is only 10 weeks, and the first three essays are in october and the second round of essays are in the beginning of december.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Lectures and tutorials are only one hour duration. I had one seminar which was 2 hours. I only had teachings 7 hours a week, which is a bit less than in UCPH. The tutorials and and seminars were mandatory and attendance was registered. However, if you could not attend, you could just write your professor and e-mail and it was fine. the tutorials are very few people (14 in one) and people are not as active during class as in UCPH. The professors are very good and open towards questions (not in lectures).

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Religion and society 
Understanding Public Policy 
Social Demography

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Religion and society - Michael, the professor, is fun and its really an interesting course learning about a bunch of different religions, without it being overly theoretical. 
Social Demography - also good, especially the tutorials, leaning a lot of excel and understanding demographics.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: transportation (bus) was quite expensive, and you cannot get around with a bike, so buscard is a must.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Groceries are cheep. Going out, same as Copenhagen (coffee, beers, dining etc)

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I joined the gym, Pleasance. Very nice gym connected to the university, only 99 pounds for the whole semester

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: everything you can think of. There's a "society" for everything

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I didn't join any, but I think the gym was good.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go around in scotland. The highlands (anywhere, but Ben y Vrackie is fun to climb), St andrews. Also go for a walk in the pentlands, arthurs seat or walk around in edinburgh - also leith.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Easy, they're so nice people.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Go to a pub :)

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Not with the scots - but there's a lot of chinese students, who keep very much to themselves. They're not easy to get to know.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Pubs.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Pack warm clothes, also for wearing at home. The apartments are very badly isolated. 
Bring enough money for going out. Best thing about Edinburgh is the pub-culture. 
Be prepared not getting a lot of local friends - you mostly get other exchange students as friends.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: It's a short semester, so get the most out of it. You're only there for 3,5 months ish. Don't stress about the exams, you'll pass no matter what!

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: getting better at speaking english and living in another country

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: living with people I didn't know beforehand.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: Drink some guinness :D

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
